audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill / Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Skill / Gnar / Gnar against a 43.97% win rate.
audit.why: Packet chart and the audited Gnar-side mirror both give Gnar Levels 1 through First item and Ryze the two-plus-item stage; the stored chart gave Gnar the late stage he does not own and hedged the early ones he does.
audit.corrected: Gnar / Gnar / Gnar / Gnar / Gnar / Gnar / Ryze, matched pairs across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].why and whys[6] both said Gnar still wins after two items, contradicting the flip.
audit.why: Seraph's plus a second mana item is where the Flux loop out-damages Mega Gnar's short window; that is the one stage Ryze owns, and both layers must say so.
audit.corrected: Two-item stage rewritten as Ryze's, keyed to taking fights away from walls.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Rune Prison as a root on demand and gives no real cooldowns for the abilities it tells you to track.
audit.why: Rune Prison roots only if Spell Flux is already on the target — otherwise it is a slow and Gnar walks out. Hop is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12 (22s at rank 1), GNAR! is 90/60/30, and Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 against Overload's 1000, which is why he out-ranges you at level 1. Ryze has no dash and Realm Warp is a delayed group portal, so a wall-stun lands unless you Flash.
audit.corrected: Flux-first stated, Hop's 22s downtime named as the trade window, and the rage bar tracked instead of a cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track his rage bar like a cooldown' was the only timing cue and no ability cooldown appeared.
audit.why: Hop's 22-second rank-1 cooldown is the punishable window that lets a full rotation complete.

edits.before: Q poke only — farm, respect everything, and bank Manaflow stacks. You're buying time, not fighting.
edits.after: Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 to your 1000 — farm at max range and bank Manaflow, do not trade.

edits.before: Seraph's online — you out-DPS and out-tank everyone in extended fights. Side-lane and Warp to every fight.
edits.after: Seraph's flips it — your loop out-DPSes Mega Gnar's window, so fight him away from every wall.

edits.before: Mega all-in near walls — track his rage bar like a cooldown. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Mega Gnar all-ins near walls; Hop is 22s at rank 1 — its downtime is when your rotation completes.

edits.before: Track Gnar’s GNAR! (Mega): Mega all-in near walls — track his rage bar like a cooldown. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track the rage bar, not a cooldown: GNAR! slams you into walls, and Rune Prison only roots through Flux — without it, it is a slow.

edits.before: His Hop (E) at level 3 lets Gnar dodge your follow-up Q after E-Flux lands, so a full Flux rotation almost never completes when he plays around the cooldown.
edits.after: His Hop (E) is 22 seconds at rank 1 and dodges your follow-up Q after E-Flux lands, so a full rotation only completes if you trade inside its downtime.

edits.before: At two items your Flux combo loops near-permanently and your teamfight damage finally matters, but Gnar still wins the 1v1 — shift to Realm Warp flanks and accept that this lane was never yours to win.
edits.after: At two items your Flux loop runs near-permanently and finally out-damages Mega Gnar's short window — take the fight away from walls so GNAR! has nothing to slam you into, and Warp in to pick him apart.

edits.before: Hold Rune Prison (W) as a response root — spend it only when Gnar hops toward you with Hop (E), never use it as poke
edits.after: Hold Rune Prison (W) for his Hop in — land Spell Flux first, or W is only a slow and he simply walks out of it

notes: Chart flipped to the packet and the audited Gnar-side mirror. The two-item stage is the one row I changed against the stored text's opinion: both phases[6].why and whys[6] previously said Gnar still wins there, which contradicted the mirror's Ryze row; I rewrote both to agree. Spell Flux is single-target per Riot's text — the kit's 'projectile' flag on E is a parsing misfire and I did not use it.
